title: Bounded inner computation
statement: Let $C,e,p\in\mathbb N$, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, and let $f$ map finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words with $|f(x)|\le C(|x|+1)^e$ for every such word $x$. For a finite Boolean word $z$, suppose $p\le 8(2C+3)(|\langle z,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle|+1)^{e+1}$, where $\mathrm{bits}(p)$ is the binary word for $p$ and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the self-delimiting pairing. The abstract computation on input $\langle z,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle$, starting in the inner scan state with registers $1$ through $14$ initialized respectively to $|\langle z,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle|$, $2|z|+2$, $2|z|$, $0$, $p$, $0$, $0$, $|\langle z,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle|+1$, $0$, $0$, $0$, $0$, $0$, and with no result recorded, halts with result $\mathbf{1}_{\{p<|q|\}}$ when $m$ is true and with the bit at position $p$ of $q$ (false if that position is absent) when $m$ is false, where $q$ is the word obtained by decoding $z$ as $(x,b)$ and returning $\langle f(x),b\rangle$ if $b$ is the canonical binary word for its decoded value, and the empty word otherwise. At every time before it halts, all register values are at most $8(2C+3)(|\langle z,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle|+1)^{e+1}$; moreover, each active instruction comparing two registers compares distinct registers, instructions comparing a register with the input word are used only on inputs of the required valid encoding (a unary prefix followed by a canonical payload, or by a pair of canonical payloads, as appropriate), and every oracle call uses a list of distinct registers.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words
For every finite Boolean word $x$, $|f(x)|\le C(|x|+1)^e$
replaced:
Let $C,e$ be natural numbers, let the mode be Boolean, and let $f$ map bit strings to
bit strings with $|f(x)|\le C(|x|+1)^e$ for every bit string $x$. For any bit string $z$
and natural number $p$ bounded by $8(2C+3)(|\langle
z,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle|+1)^{e+1}$, the machine, started in its inner scan state on
input $\langle z,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle$ with the specified register values, halts with
the bit indicating whether $p$ is less than the length of the transformed paired word
when the mode is true, and otherwise with the bit at position $p$ of that transformed
word (taking missing positions to be false). The transformed word is obtained by parsing
$z$ as a pair $(x,b)$ and returning $\langle f(x),b\rangle$ when $b$ is the canonical
binary representation of its decoded value, and the empty word otherwise.
